=== AGENTS.md
# AGENTS.md

Monize is a personal finance manager (a Microsoft Money replacement). Four layers, each with its own `package.json`: `backend/` (NestJS + TypeORM), `frontend/` (Next.js App Router + React, Tailwind v4, Zustand), `database/` (`schema.sql` plus `migrations/`, PostgreSQL 16), `e2e/` (Playwright). `docs/` holds the cross-layer contracts, `helm/` the chart, `scripts/` the repo-level CI checks. Everything runs in Docker: `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up`.

This is the canonical instruction file for every coding agent; `CLAUDE.md` imports it and adds only what Claude Code specifically should do. It holds the repo-wide rules and the workflow. The layer files `backend/CLAUDE.md` and `frontend/CLAUDE.md` are indexes over `docs/backend/` and `docs/frontend/`; `database/CLAUDE.md` and `e2e/CLAUDE.md` are short. Read the layer file for the layer you touch, then only the documents its table sends you to.

## How the instruction files are organised

This file and the layer files are read on every task, so they hold only what nearly every task needs, each rule in one or two sentences naming the thing to use and the thing not to.

- **Reading.** Before working in a layer, read its `CLAUDE.md`, then only the rows of its "Read when the work touches it" table that match the task.
- **Writing a rule.** A new rule is one line in the layer index (or one sentence in this file) plus the full entry in the matching `docs/<layer>/*.md` or contract document. If it does not fit in a sentence, it belongs in `docs/`.
- **Never in an instruction file:** the history of the defect, issue and PR numbers, the mechanism of the guard that holds the rule, edge cases, worked examples. Those go in the `docs/` entry, the regression test's comment, or an ADR.
- **A rule the machine enforces needs no essay.** Where a type, a lint rule or a source-scanning test holds a rule, name the abstraction to use and stop; the guard's failure message says what to use instead. `docs/guard-tests.md` says how to write one. `backend/src/common/instruction-files.spec.ts` holds every instruction file under its size ceiling and every `docs/<layer>/*.md` reachable from its index.

## Commands

Run from the layer directory.

```bash
# backend/
npm run lint && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run typecheck   # lint, src-only tsc, tsc over src AND test
npm run test:unit -- <pattern>                            # Jest, src/**/*.spec.ts, no database; npm test takes no args
TZ=UTC npm run test:unit -- --coverage                    # what CI runs (95/94/95/85 thresholds)
npm run test:integration                                  # test/integration/*.spec.ts, real PostgreSQL, one worker
npm run migration:lint:test && npm run migration:lint     # migrations touched
npm run push:client:test && npm run push:tls:test         # backend/scripts push tooling touched
npm run i18n:pseudo && npm run i18n:check                 # after editing en/*.json (not a CI gate for the backend)

# frontend/
npm run lint && npm run type-check && npm run i18n:check
npm run test -- <pattern>                                 # focused; CI runs test:cov (91/90/87/85 thresholds)
npm run test:cov && npm run build                         # the gate; bundle size is checked on every PR

# e2e/  (stack: docker compose -f docker-compose.e2e.yml up -d --wait)
npm test -- --workers=1                                   # whole suite; a single spec file is safe without the flag
npm run test:push                                         # push suite, playwright.push.config.ts, needs no stack

# repo root
node scripts/check-env-docs.mjs                           # a new process.env / configService.get must be in .env.example
node scripts/check-docs-manifests.mjs                     # a doc naming a path, an npm script or a Helm default
node scripts/check-migration-prefixes.mjs                 # needs the base ref (full clone), silently skips in a shallow one
scripts/verify-schema.sh                                  # migrations replay as a no-op on schema.sql; Docker only
```

## Required before you push

Mirrors `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. While developing run `npm run test:changed` (changed specs plus every guard, failures only); the coverage gate is CI's, run it locally only when asked.

- `backend/`: the three lint/typecheck commands, `npm run test:changed`, plus `migration:lint` when a migration changed and `npm run build && npm run test:integration` when a query, an entity, a migration or an RLS context changed.
- `frontend/`: `lint`, `type-check`, `i18n:check`, `test:changed`, `build`.
- A migration or `database/schema.sql`: `migration:lint`, `scripts/verify-schema.sh`, `node scripts/check-migration-prefixes.mjs`.
- An env var, a documented path or a Helm default: the two `scripts/check-*.mjs` above.
- A control an E2E spec drives was renamed or removed: grep `e2e/` for its accessible name; no unit suite loads those specs.
- **Stage new files first.** The guards that walk the tree with `git ls-files` cannot see an untracked file (`git add -N` is enough); green before staging and red in CI is not a flake.
- CI pulls images from `mirror.gcr.io` or `ghcr.io`, never Docker Hub (`ci-images.guard.spec.ts`).
- CI runs in UTC with one worker. The backend's database-backed suites rebuild one shared `monize_test` and never run in parallel with anything, including each other. `docs/verification-contract.md` section 7 explains the rest.
- The pre-commit hook (husky + lint-staged) runs `eslint --max-warnings=0 --fix` and prettier on staged files, which is stricter than CI's `lint`: a warning blocks the commit.

## Conventions you cannot infer from the code

- **`database/schema.sql` changes in the same commit as every migration.** New migrations are `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description.sql`; the checklist is in `database/CLAUDE.md`.
- **A guard test is met by fixing the code.** Baselines, allowlists and grandfather lists are shrink-only. If a guard fires and you believe it is wrong, stop and report what it names.
- No emojis anywhere, including commit messages and PR bodies. No `console.log`; the NestJS `Logger`. Immutability always. Many small files (200-400 lines typical, 800 max), organized by feature.
- **Security, do not regress:** parameterized SQL only; controllers under `AuthGuard('jwt')`; `userId` from the JWT, never from the request; `ParseUUIDPipe` on `:id`; DTOs with `whitelist` + `forbidNonWhitelisted` and bounded fields; `escapeHtml()` on every user value in an email template; secrets encrypted (AES-256-GCM) and never returned to the client.

## Internationalization (every change)

Every user-facing string is translated: `useTranslations` on the client, `tr(key, fallback, args)` for exception messages and `emailTranslator(i18n, recipientLang)` for anything composed outside a request on the server. Develop English-first, regenerate the pseudo-locale with `npm run i18n:pseudo`, and translate every other locale as the final commit on the PR; never hand-edit `xx/*`. The locale lists in `frontend/src/i18n/config.ts` and `backend/src/i18n/config.ts` stay in sync. Grep for a key before adding it: `JSON.parse` keeps the last duplicate. A number a person reads is localized by its own preference, `useNumberFormat()` on the client and `backend/src/common/number-locale.util.ts` on the server (`docs/frontend/forms-and-formatting.md`).

## Database access (CRITICAL)

**All** database access goes through `withScopedDb` (`backend/src/common/db/scoped-db.ts`), the single RLS-compliant door. Never add an `@InjectRepository(...)` field, a `this.dataSource.createQueryRunner()` call, a `this.dataSource.transaction(...)` call, or a bare `this.dataSource.query(...)`; ESLint bans the first three (`backend/eslint.config.mjs`). `DataSource.transaction()` is banned for a reason the `createQueryRunner()` ban did not cover: it opens a transaction that knows nothing about the ambient scoped manager, so it carries no identity GUCs under enforcement and commits independently of the caller's rollback. Inject `DataSource`; get repositories from the transaction's `EntityManager`; helpers take an `EntityManager`, never a query runner.

```typescript
await withScopedDb(this.dataSource, async (m) => {
  const repo = m.getRepository(UserPreference);
  const row = await repo.findOne({ where: { userId } });
  // ...mutate + repo.save(row); every query shares the transaction and the tenant GUC.
});
```

`withScopedDb` throws without an ambient identity. Authenticated routes have one (`RequestContextInterceptor`); everything else seeds its own from `backend/src/common/db/with-context.ts`: `withUserContext(userId, fn)` for a cron's per-user body, a background write or a bearer-only route; `withSystemContext(fn)` for genuinely cross-user work (fan-outs, seeders, bootstrap hooks, admin); `withDelegateContext(owner, delegate, fn)` where the two ids must differ; `withPreserveTimestamps(fn)` only in the backup restore. A new call site of any of these is added to `WITH_CONTEXT_ALLOWLIST` in the same PR, as a reviewed decision. Nested `withScopedDb` calls join the ambient transaction, so a service calling another is safe. `docs/row-level-security-contract.md` is canonical for exempt tables and the one sanctioned direct-`DataSource` exception; `docs/backend/database-access-and-tenancy.md` has the details and the "whose row is it" table.

## Transactions (CRITICAL)

Any operation that touches multiple tables or does read-modify-write runs in one `withScopedDb` transaction; this is the most common source of bugs in this codebase. **A rejected command must not already have written**: every check that can refuse a request (ownership, tenant or scenario identity, revision, precondition) runs inside the same transaction as the mutation, under the same lock where concurrency matters. Pass the caller's expectation down so the operation can refuse before writing. `docs/financial-calculation-contract.md` section 7 has the rule and the test obligation.

## Financial math

Money is `decimal(20,4)`. In JavaScript, never accumulate floats: sum `Math.round(Number(x) * 10000)` and divide once, or `roundMoney` every result, including a delta (`newAmount - oldAmount` is what a balance moves by). Balance updates are atomic SQL: `UPDATE accounts SET current_balance = current_balance + $1 WHERE id = $2`.

One sentence each; the reasoning and the guard that holds each one are in the contract documents.

- **An exchange rate is not money.** Rates are `NUMERIC(20,10)`: `roundFxRate`, never `roundMoney` or `toFixed(4)`; convert with `applyFxConversion`, validate with `normalizeFxEntry` (`backend/src/common/fx-entry.util.ts`).
- **A rate for a date is `resolveFxRate`** (`backend/src/common/time-series/fx-rate-resolver.ts`): the newest observation on or before the date within `FX_MAX_RATE_AGE_DAYS`, never one struck after it and never an unboundedly old one; `null` otherwise. INV-FX-001.
- **Rate 1 means "same currency", never "no rate found".** A failed lookup is unknown, not `1` and not the unconverted amount. Aggregate through `FxAggregate` (`backend/src/common/fx-aggregate.ts`); its `total` is `null` while `knownSubtotal` carries what converted.
- **A currency code is derived from the account**, never accepted from the request: `assertTransactionCurrencyMatchesAccount`.
- **A row carrying its own rate is converted at that rate on every surface**; the market rate on its own date is the fallback and the surface says which it used. INV-FX-002.
- **An executed total is the fact and the per-share price is derived from it** (`backend/src/securities/investment-amount.util.ts`), never the reverse on an unchanged row. INV-TRADE-001.
- **A preview computes what the commit will do, through the same code.** Call the same resolver from both.
- **Ask which occurrence before asking how much.** Every surface reads a scheduled occurrence from `ScheduledOccurrenceService` (client: `nextOccurrenceEffectiveAmount`, `nextOccurrenceDueDate`, `occurrenceSettlementAccountId`), never `amount`, `nextDueDate`, `accountId` or `nextOverride?.amount ?? amount`. `null` means unknown and is never a licence to fall back to the snapshot. INV-OCCURRENCE-003.
- **The fix for one surface is not the fix.** When you fix a derived-figure defect, grep every consumer of the raw field (dashboard, reports, exports, AI assistant, MCP, notifications) in the same commit and give them one server-authoritative answer.
- **A daily change needs a current close, not only the last two.** Two stored closes are a day's move only while they are adjacent sessions and the newer one is current: `resolveDailyPriceChange` (`backend/src/securities/daily-change.util.ts`), never a subtraction of the two most recent rows; a refusal is `null` and the surface names the session it does have.
- **A board of movers is one session's.** A ranked list of daily moves keeps only the rows carrying the newest `priceDate` on it (`keepNewestSession`, same file), so a holding whose feed skipped today does not rank yesterday's move against today's; a per-security readout dates each row instead.
- **A period change is not a return.** `PortfolioPeriodResultService` answers `valueChange`, `netExternalFlows` and `investmentResult` as three figures and puts a percentage only over the result; a difference of two closes counts the reader's own deposits as performance. INV-PORTRESULT-001.
- **Cash is not an investment.** A figure captioned as what the INVESTMENTS earned is `investmentPnl` / `investmentReturnPercent` over `securitiesValue` alone, never a measure that holds idle cash in its base. INV-PORTRESULT-002.
- **Convert before summing.** `FxAggregate` on the server, `sumConverted` / `sumEffectiveOccurrences` on the client; a total names its currency; a missing rate and an unknown component are two different reports with two different repairs.
- **The reporting-currency fallback is one constant.** `preferredCurrency` / `resolveUserDefaultCurrency` on the server, `preferredCurrency` on the client, `FALLBACK_DEFAULT_CURRENCY` the only literal per layer.
- **Withholding a figure is only honest if the reader learns why, and what to do.** A message that a figure cannot be worked out names the exact thing that is missing (the security, the currency pair, the account, the dates) and where the reader obtains it; where a provider can supply it, the read path fetches it first and discloses only what is still missing; a request that failed or has not answered is said to be one, never shown as missing data. A bare `null` is a dead end. `docs/financial-calculation-contract.md` section 1.3.
- **A subtotal is not a total (CRITICAL).** A field named `total*`, `portfolioValue`, `gain`, `tax` or `estimated*` carries a value only when every component is known; otherwise it is `null` and the partial sum, if returned, goes in its own named field. Never default a price, cost basis or rate to `0` or `1`. **`null` is not the safe answer either**: empty accounts hold zero, move zero, owe zero. Decide which of the two each branch is in before writing it.
- **A completeness flag is read where the numbers are shown.** Track each cause (`fxComplete`, `pricesComplete`), give consumers one `valuationComplete`, carry it to every surface including the LLM shape, read it as `=== false` (absent means no information), and relabel a partial figure rather than leaving a total's caption over it. Zero needs no rate.
- **VOID means no balance moved, on every path that writes one**; inclusion is decided per row, and a cross-owner transfer's legs may hold different statuses. INV-TRANSFER-001.
- **A refusal is only worth as much as its least-guarded entry point.** When you refuse a state on one path, grep the bulk, AI-action and MCP routes to the same write in the same commit.
- **A deletion reverses only what the row contributed**: `deletionBalanceEffect` (`backend/src/common/deletion-balance.util.ts`), never a hand-rolled `-Number(row.amount)`.
- **A balance change is not finished until derived state is invalidated.** A helper returns the accounts it moved; the recompute is dispatched after the commit, never inside the transaction. INV-CACHE-001.
- **A change is a value difference, not a field being present.** Forms resend every field; compare against the row before repricing or re-resolving anything.
- **A share-count replay is written once**: `applyActionToQuantity` / `acquisitionCost` (`backend/src/securities/investment-replay.util.ts`).
- **A category's cost is its signed sum over rows of both signs**, netted within one category: `isNetSpending` / `NET_SPEND_AMOUNT` on the server, `netEntityTotal` on the client; never `totalIncome` or `totalExpenses` alone.
- **What a row is decides a report's filter, never its account type.** `investmentExclusionSql` / `applyInvestmentTransactionFilters` and `reportableTransactionAmountSql` (`backend/src/common/investment-filter.util.ts`). INV-REPORT-001.

The layer files `backend/CLAUDE.md` and `frontend/CLAUDE.md` are indexes over `docs/backend/` and `docs/frontend/`; `database/CLAUDE.md` and `e2e/CLAUDE.md` are short. Read the layer file for the layer you touch, then only the documents its table sends you to.

## How the instruction files are organised

This file and the layer files are read on every task, so they hold only what nearly every task needs, each rule in one or two sentences naming the thing to use and the thing not to.

- **Reading.** Before working in a layer, read its `CLAUDE.md`, then only the rows of its "Read when the work touches it" table that match the task.
- **Writing a rule.** A new rule is one line in the layer index (or one sentence in this file) plus the full entry in the matching `docs/<layer>/*.md` or contract document. If it does not fit in a sentence, it belongs in `docs/`.
- **Never in an instruction file:** the history of the defect, issue and PR numbers, the mechanism of the guard that holds the rule, edge cases, worked examples. Those go in the `docs/` entry, the regression test's comment, or an ADR.
- **A rule the machine enforces needs no essay.** Where a type, a lint rule or a source-scanning test holds a rule, name the abstraction to use and stop; the guard's failure message says what to use instead. `docs/guard-tests.md` says how to write one. `backend/src/common/instruction-files.spec.ts` holds every instruction file under its size ceiling and every `docs/<layer>/*.md` reachable from its index.

## Commands

Run from the layer directory.

```bash
# backend/
npm run lint && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run typecheck   # lint, src-only tsc, tsc over src AND test
npm run test:unit -- <pattern>                            # Jest, src/**/*.spec.ts, no database; npm test takes no args
TZ=UTC npm run test:unit -- --coverage                    # what CI runs (95/94/95/85 thresholds)
npm run test:integration                                  # test/integration/*.spec.ts, real PostgreSQL, one worker
npm run migration:lint:test && npm run migration:lint     # migrations touched
npm run push:client:test && npm run push:tls:test         # backend/scripts push tooling touched
npm run i18n:pseudo && npm run i18n:check                 # after editing en/*.json (not a CI gate for the backend)

# frontend/
npm run lint && npm run type-check && npm run i18n:check
npm run test -- <pattern>                                 # focused; CI runs test:cov (91/90/87/85 thresholds)
npm run test:cov && npm run build                         # the gate; bundle size is checked on every PR

# e2e/  (stack: docker compose -f docker-compose.e2e.yml up -d --wait)
npm test -- --workers=1                                   # whole suite; a single spec file is safe without the flag
npm run test:push                                         # push suite, playwright.push.config.ts, needs no stack

# repo root
node scripts/check-env-docs.mjs                           # a new process.env / configService.get must be in .env.example
node scripts/check-docs-manifests.mjs                     # a doc naming a path, an npm script or a Helm default
node scripts/check-migration-prefixes.mjs                 # needs the base ref (full clone), silently skips in a shallow one
scripts/verify-schema.sh                                  # migrations replay as a no-op on schema.sql; Docker only
```

## Required before you push

Mirrors `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. While developing run `npm run test:changed` (changed specs plus every guard, failures only); the coverage gate is CI's, run it locally only when asked.

- `backend/`: the three lint/typecheck commands, `npm run test:changed`, plus `migration:lint` when a migration changed and `npm run build && npm run test:integration` when a query, an entity, a migration or an RLS context changed.
- `frontend/`: `lint`, `type-check`, `i18n:check`, `test:changed`, `build`.
- A migration or `database/schema.sql`: `migration:lint`, `scripts/verify-schema.sh`, `node scripts/check-migration-prefixes.mjs`.
- An env var, a documented path or a Helm default: the two `scripts/check-*.mjs` above.
- A control an E2E spec drives was renamed or removed: grep `e2e/` for its accessible name; no unit suite loads those specs.
- **Stage new files first.** The guards that walk the tree with `git ls-files` cannot see an untracked file (`git add -N` is enough); green before staging and red in CI is not a flake.
- CI pulls images from `mirror.gcr.io` or `ghcr.io`, never Docker Hub (`ci-images.guard.spec.ts`).
- CI runs in UTC with one worker. The backend's database-backed suites rebuild one shared `monize_test` and never run in parallel with anything, including each other. `docs/verification-contract.md` section 7 explains the rest.
- The pre-commit hook (husky + lint-staged) runs `eslint --max-warnings=0 --fix` and prettier on staged files, which is stricter than CI's `lint`: a warning blocks the commit.

## Conventions you cannot infer from the code

- **`database/schema.sql` changes in the same commit as every migration.** New migrations are `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description.sql`; the checklist is in `database/CLAUDE.md`.
- **A guard test is met by fixing the code.** Baselines, allowlists and grandfather lists are shrink-only. If a guard fires and you believe it is wrong, stop and report what it names.
- No emojis anywhere, including commit messages and PR bodies. No `console.log`; the NestJS `Logger`. Immutability always. Many small files (200-400 lines typical, 800 max), organized by feature.
- **Security, do not regress:** parameterized SQL only; controllers under `AuthGuard('jwt')`; `userId` from the JWT, never from the request; `ParseUUIDPipe` on `:id`; DTOs with `whitelist` + `forbidNonWhitelisted` and bounded fields; `escapeHtml()` on every user value in an email template; secrets encrypted (AES-256-GCM) and never returned to the client.

## Internationalization (every change)

Every user-facing string is translated: `useTranslations` on the client, `tr(key, fallback, args)` for exception messages and `emailTranslator(i18n, recipientLang)` for anything composed outside a request on the server. Develop English-first, regenerate the pseudo-locale with `npm run i18n:pseudo`, and translate every other locale as the final commit on the PR; never hand-edit `xx/*`. The locale lists in `frontend/src/i18n/config.ts` and `backend/src/i18n/config.ts` stay in sync. Grep for a key before adding it: `JSON.parse` keeps the last duplicate. A number a person reads is localized by its own preference, `useNumberFormat()` on the client and `backend/src/common/number-locale.util.ts` on the server (`docs/frontend/forms-and-formatting.md`).

## Database access (CRITICAL)

**All** database access goes through `withScopedDb` (`backend/src/common/db/scoped-db.ts`), the single RLS-compliant door. Never add an `@InjectRepository(...)` field, a `this.dataSource.createQueryRunner()` call, a `this.dataSource.transaction(...)` call, or a bare `this.dataSource.query(...)`; ESLint bans the first three (`backend/eslint.config.mjs`). `DataSource.transaction()` is banned for a reason the `createQueryRunner()` ban did not cover: it opens a transaction that knows nothing about the ambient scoped manager, so it carries no identity GUCs under enforcement and commits independently of the caller's rollback. Inject `DataSource`; get repositories from the transaction's `EntityManager`; helpers take an `EntityManager`, never a query runner.

```typescript
await withScopedDb(this.dataSource, async (m) => {
  const repo = m.getRepository(UserPreference);
  const row = await repo.findOne({ where: { userId } });
  // ...mutate + repo.save(row); every query shares the transaction and the tenant GUC.
});
```

`withScopedDb` throws without an ambient identity. Authenticated routes have one (`RequestContextInterceptor`); everything else seeds its own from `backend/src/common/db/with-context.ts`: `withUserContext(userId, fn)` for a cron's per-user body, a background write or a bearer-only route; `withSystemContext(fn)` for genuinely cross-user work (fan-outs, seeders, bootstrap hooks, admin); `withDelegateContext(owner, delegate, fn)` where the two ids must differ; `withPreserveTimestamps(fn)` only in the backup restore. A new call site of any of these is added to `WITH_CONTEXT_ALLOWLIST` in the same PR, as a reviewed decision. Nested `withScopedDb` calls join the ambient transaction, so a service calling another is safe. `docs/row-level-security-contract.md` is canonical for exempt tables and the one sanctioned direct-`DataSource` exception; `docs/backend/database-access-and-tenancy.md` has the details and the "whose row is it" table.

## Transactions (CRITICAL)

Any operation that touches multiple tables or does read-modify-write runs in one `withScopedDb` transaction; this is the most common source of bugs in this codebase. **A rejected command must not already have written**: every check that can refuse a request (ownership, tenant or scenario identity, revision, precondition) runs inside the same transaction as the mutation, under the same lock where concurrency matters. Pass the caller's expectation down so the operation can refuse before writing. `docs/financial-calculation-contract.md` section 7 has the rule and the test obligation.

## Financial math

Money is `decimal(20,4)`. In JavaScript, never accumulate floats: sum `Math.round(Number(x) * 10000)` and divide once, or `roundMoney` every result, including a delta (`newAmount - oldAmount` is what a balance moves by). Balance updates are atomic SQL: `UPDATE accounts SET current_balance = current_balance + $1 WHERE id = $2`.

One sentence each; the reasoning and the guard that holds each one are in the contract documents.

- **An exchange rate is not money.** Rates are `NUMERIC(20,10)`: `roundFxRate`, never `roundMoney` or `toFixed(4)`; convert with `applyFxConversion`, validate with `normalizeFxEntry` (`backend/src/common/fx-entry.util.ts`).
- **A rate for a date is `resolveFxRate`** (`backend/src/common/time-series/fx-rate-resolver.ts`): the newest observation on or before the date within `FX_MAX_RATE_AGE_DAYS`, never one struck after it and never an unboundedly old one; `null` otherwise. INV-FX-001.
- **Rate 1 means "same currency", never "no rate found".** A failed lookup is unknown, not `1` and not the unconverted amount. Aggregate through `FxAggregate` (`backend/src/common/fx-aggregate.ts`); its `total` is `null` while `knownSubtotal` carries what converted.
- **A currency code is derived from the account**, never accepted from the request: `assertTransactionCurrencyMatchesAccount`.
- **A row carrying its own rate is converted at that rate on every surface**; the market rate on its own date is the fallback and the surface says which it used. INV-FX-002.
- **An executed total is the fact and the per-share price is derived from it** (`backend/src/securities/investment-amount.util.ts`), never the reverse on an unchanged row. INV-TRADE-001.
- **A preview computes what the commit will do, through the same code.** Call the same resolver from both.
- **Ask which occurrence before asking how much.** Every surface reads a scheduled occurrence from `ScheduledOccurrenceService` (client: `nextOccurrenceEffectiveAmount`, `nextOccurrenceDueDate`, `occurrenceSettlementAccountId`), never `amount`, `nextDueDate`, `accountId` or `nextOverride?.amount ?? amount`. `null` means unknown and is never a licence to fall back to the snapshot. INV-OCCURRENCE-003.
- **The fix for one surface is not the fix.** When you fix a derived-figure defect, grep every consumer of the raw field (dashboard, reports, exports, AI assistant, MCP, notifications) in the same commit and give them one server-authoritative answer.
- **A daily change needs a current close, not only the last two.** Two stored closes are a day's move only while they are adjacent sessions and the newer one is current: `resolveDailyPriceChange` (`backend/src/securities/daily-change.util.ts`), never a subtraction of the two most recent rows; a refusal is `null` and the surface names the session it does have.
- **A board of movers is one session's.** A ranked list of daily moves keeps only the rows carrying the newest `priceDate` on it (`keepNewestSession`, same file), so a holding whose feed skipped today does not rank yesterday's move against today's; a per-security readout dates each row instead.
- **A period change is not a return.** `PortfolioPeriodResultService` answers `valueChange`, `netExternalFlows` and `investmentResult` as three figures and puts a percentage only over the result; a difference of two closes counts the reader's own deposits as performance. INV-PORTRESULT-001.
- **Cash is not an investment.** A figure captioned as what the INVESTMENTS earned is `investmentPnl` / `investmentReturnPercent` over `securitiesValue` alone, never a measure that holds idle cash in its base. INV-PORTRESULT-002.
- **Convert before summing.** `FxAggregate` on the server, `sumConverted` / `sumEffectiveOccurrences` on the client; a total names its currency; a missing rate and an unknown component are two different reports with two different repairs.
- **The reporting-currency fallback is one constant.** `preferredCurrency` / `resolveUserDefaultCurrency` on the server, `preferredCurrency` on the client, `FALLBACK_DEFAULT_CURRENCY` the only literal per layer.
- **Withholding a figure is only honest if the reader learns why, and what to do.** A message that a figure cannot be worked out names the exact thing that is missing (the security, the currency pair, the account, the dates) and where the reader obtains it; where a provider can supply it, the read path fetches it first and discloses only what is still missing; a request that failed or has not answered is said to be one, never shown as missing data. A bare `null` is a dead end. `docs/financial-calculation-contract.md` section 1.3.
- **A subtotal is not a total (CRITICAL).** A field named `total*`, `portfolioValue`, `gain`, `tax` or `estimated*` carries a value only when every component is known; otherwise it is `null` and the partial sum, if returned, goes in its own named field. Never default a price, cost basis or rate to `0` or `1`. **`null` is not the safe answer either**: empty accounts hold zero, move zero, owe zero. Decide which of the two each branch is in before writing it.
- **A completeness flag is read where the numbers are shown.** Track each cause (`fxComplete`, `pricesComplete`), give consumers one `valuationComplete`, carry it to every surface including the LLM shape, read it as `=== false` (absent means no information), and relabel a partial figure rather than leaving a total's caption over it. Zero needs no rate.
- **VOID means no balance moved, on every path that writes one**; inclusion is decided per row, and a cross-owner transfer's legs may hold different statuses. INV-TRANSFER-001.
- **A refusal is only worth as much as its least-guarded entry point.** When you refuse a state on one path, grep the bulk, AI-action and MCP routes to the same write in the same commit.
- **A deletion reverses only what the row contributed**: `deletionBalanceEffect` (`backend/src/common/deletion-balance.util.ts`), never a hand-rolled `-Number(row.amount)`.
- **A balance change is not finished until derived state is invalidated.** A helper returns the accounts it moved; the recompute is dispatched after the commit, never inside the transaction. INV-CACHE-001.
- **A change is a value difference, not a field being present.** Forms resend every field; compare against the row before repricing or re-resolving anything.
- **A share-count replay is written once**: `applyActionToQuantity` / `acquisitionCost` (`backend/src/securities/investment-replay.util.ts`).
- **A category's cost is its signed sum over rows of both signs**, netted within one category: `isNetSpending` / `NET_SPEND_AMOUNT` on the server, `netEntityTotal` on the client; never `totalIncome` or `totalExpenses` alone.
- **What a row is decides a report's filter, never its account type.** `investmentExclusionSql` / `applyInvestmentTransactionFilters` and `reportableTransactionAmountSql` (`backend/src/common/investment-filter.util.ts`). INV-REPORT-001.

# Monize: issue drafts, round 2026-11-02-93f4e68-review

Target: kenlasko/monize, `main` at `93f4e68` (2026-11-03 02:47 UTC). No dev branch; releases come from `main`. The repo has no issue template, so the §5 form is used as is. Nothing here is filed until Garrett says go for the batch. Four drafts (cap is six).

Duplicate check (read-only `gh api search/issues`, 2026-11-03): queries `payee delete`, `delete payee transactions`, `category delete budget`, `reconciled date`, `reconciled_date`, `timezone day`, `reassign parameters`, `bind message`, `delete category` returned no issue or PR describing any of the four below. #1931/#1935 (remove a category from a budget) and #1754 (loan interest category required) are adjacent and make MZ-L01 more consequential, not duplicates. #1911 fixed an auto-post timezone case, not the reconcile stamp.

---

## Draft 1 (MZ-L01)

**Title:** [Bug] Deleting an unused category silently deletes its payroll deduction rules and blanks its budget lines and loan category links

**Version:** `main` at `93f4e68`.

**Summary:** `CategoriesService.remove` refuses a delete only when `getTransactionCount` is non-zero, and that count covers transactions, transaction splits, scheduled transactions and scheduled splits (`backend/src/categories/categories.service.ts:654-698`). The schema has more tables pointing at `categories`: `payroll_deduction_rules.category_id` is `ON DELETE CASCADE` (`database/schema.sql:3640`); `budget_categories.category_id` and `budget_period_categories.category_id` are `ON DELETE SET NULL` (`schema.sql:2424`, `2472`); the loan columns `accounts.principal_category_id`, `interest_category_id`, `overpayment_category_id`, `asset_category_id` are `ON DELETE SET NULL` (`schema.sql:1197-1207`); so are `scheduled_transaction_overrides.category_id` (`schema.sql:1222`) and `shared_postings.category_id` (`schema.sql:4722`). None of them is counted, so a category with no transactions deletes cleanly and the database quietly removes or detaches those rows.

**Result:** a payroll deduction rule disappears with no message; a budget keeps a line that now reads "Uncategorized" (`budgets/budget-spending.util.ts:411-421`) and can never match spending again; a loan or mortgage whose interest category was required at setup (`accounts/loan-mortgage-account.service.ts:251`, `426`) is left with `interest_category_id = NULL`, which the setup path itself refuses.

**Where:** `backend/src/categories/categories.service.ts:579-651`, `654-698`; `database/schema.sql:3640`, `2424`, `2472`, `1197-1207`, `1222`, `4722`.

**Steps:**
1. Create a category "Union dues" with no transactions.
2. Add a payroll deduction rule for it, and add it to a budget.
3. Delete the category from the Categories page.
4. *Expected:* the delete is refused with a count of what still uses the category (as it is for transactions), or the referencers are listed for reassignment.
   *Actual:* the delete succeeds; the payroll deduction rule is gone and the budget line reads "Uncategorized".

**How this was found:** an AI-assisted review of the source, confirmed by reading the code and the schema. Not reproduced in the running app, so the steps above are what the code says will happen.

**Related:** the referencer count also runs in its own transaction before the deleting one (`categories.service.ts:600-608` vs `630-641`), so a transaction saved in between keeps its row and loses its category through `transactions.category_id ON DELETE SET NULL` (`schema.sql:387`) with no refusal; `accounts.delete` already re-checks under the lock inside the deleting transaction (`accounts.service.ts:2238-2248`) for the same reason.

**Possible fix:** count every table whose foreign key points at `categories` (or let one query over `information_schema.referential_constraints` drive it), do the count inside the deleting transaction, and refuse with the breakdown. A test that creates a category used only by a payroll rule and only by a budget line, deletes it, and expects a refusal in both cases would catch this.

---

## Draft 2 (MZ-L02)

**Title:** [Bug] Reconciling near midnight stamps the reconciled date with the server's day, not the user's

**Version:** `main` at `93f4e68`.

**Summary:** `applyStatusTransition` sets `fields.reconciledDate = formatDateYMDLocal(new Date())` (`backend/src/transactions/transaction-reconciliation.service.ts:167`), which is the backend process's local calendar day (UTC in the shipped containers). Five lines later the same write decides whether the row is future-dated with `isTransactionInFuture(locked.transactionDate)` (`:172`), which goes through `todayYMD()` and the request's timezone (`common/date-utils.ts:124-135`). 2. At 07:30 Tokyo time, reconcile a transaction dated today.

**Related:** `net-worth/net-worth.service.ts:2849`, `2937` and `securities/portfolio-calculation.service.ts:681`, `2586` bound monthly sums and holdings by `CURRENT_DATE` too, so the net-worth and portfolio figures can disagree with the account balance for the same hours.

**Possible fix:** pass the user's day as a parameter to both recomputes (the import runs under the importing user's context; the undo under the acting user's), or call `recalculateCurrentBalance` itself, as the comment says it does. A test that fixes the clock at 02:00 UTC, sets the request timezone to America/Toronto, creates a row dated the user's tomorrow and runs undo and import post-processing, asserting the balance excludes it, would catch it.

---

## Draft 4 (MZ-L04)

**Title:** [Bug] Reassigning or deleting a category fails for a user with more than about 65,000 transactions

**Version:** `main` at `93f4e68`.

**Summary:** `CategoriesService.reassignTransactions` selects the id of every transaction the user owns (`backend/src/categories/categories.service.ts:721-727`) and binds the whole list into the next statement with `transactionId IN (:...transactionIds)` (`:738`). TypeORM expands that into one bind parameter per id, and the PostgreSQL wire protocol carries the parameter count in 16 bits, so the statement fails once the user has 65,535 or more transactions. The scheduled-split count and update do the same with schedule ids (`:674-690`, `:749-766`), at a far higher threshold. The list exists only to scope the splits to the user's transactions, which the `transactions` join already does.

**Result:** for a long Microsoft Money or Quicken history (the import this app is built for), "reassign transactions" for a category errors out, and because `remove` requires a zero count, the category can be neither emptied nor deleted. The message is a database error, not a domain one.

**Where:** `backend/src/categories/categories.service.ts:721-741`; `674-690`, `749-766`.

**Steps:**
1. Import a history of 70,000 transactions (any account mix).
2. Categories, pick any category, Reassign transactions to another category.
3. *Expected:* the rows move.
   *Actual:* the request fails with a database error (bind parameter count), and the category cannot be deleted afterwards either.

**How this was found:** an AI-assisted review of the source, confirmed by reading the code. Not reproduced in the running app, so the steps above are what the code says will happen.

**Possible fix:** replace the id list with a subquery or join on `transaction.userId` (`UPDATE transaction_splits SET category_id = ... FROM transactions t WHERE t.id = split.transaction_id AND t.user_id = $1 AND split.category_id = $2`), and the same for scheduled splits. A test that seeds 66,000 transactions for one user and reassigns a category would catch it; a lighter guard test could forbid `IN (:...` fed by a `getMany()` over all of a user's rows.

---

## Not filing

- **MZ-L05, payee delete has no referencer check (stuck).** `PayeesService.remove` (`payees.service.ts:1280-1308`) deletes without counting; `transactions.payee_id` and `scheduled_transactions.payee_id` have no `ON DELETE` action (`schema.sql:385`, `1084`), so the database refuses and the HTTP filter turns code 23503 into a generic 400 "Referenced record does not exist or cannot be removed" (`http-error-body.ts:125`). Nothing is lost; the user is left without a count or a pointer to Merge, on the REST, AI batch (`ai-actions.service.ts:716-718`) and MCP (`payees.tool.ts:604`, `656`, `750`) doors alike. §4 keeps `stuck` in the ledger.
- **MZ-L06, category delete count-then-delete race (wrong-result).** Same door as Draft 1; carried in its *Related* line rather than filed twice.
- **MZ-L07, import moves the balance for VOID and future rows (process).** `import-regular-processor.service.ts:154` adds every row's amount before its status matters; the post-import recompute (`import-post-processing.service.ts:44-112`) corrects it in the normal case and only logs when it fails. The repo's own rule ("VOID means no balance moved, on every path that writes one") is broken in form, not, in the usual run, in effect. Ledger only.

# Monize, round 2026-11-02-93f4e68-review (file mode)

Target: kenlasko/monize, `main` at `93f4e68` (committed 2026-11-03 02:47 UTC; re-checked unchanged before the drafts were written). Clone: partial, read only, nothing installed, built or run from it. Probes: one, standard library only, outside the clone. Time box: 2 hours from clone to drafts (FILING §9). Nothing filed; drafts in `2026-11-02-93f4e68-review-issues.md` await Garrett's go.

## 1. One line

7 findings: 1 data-loss, 3 wrong-result, 1 crash, 1 stuck, 1 process; 1 reproduced (probe), 6 by reading. 4 drafted for filing, 3 held in the ledger.

## 2. Findings, worst first

**MZ-L01, deleting an unused category silently deletes payroll deduction rules and blanks budget lines and loan category links.** data-loss, reading. `backend/src/categories/categories.service.ts:579-651` refuses only on `getTransactionCount` (654-698), which counts transactions, splits, schedules and schedule splits. The schema also points `payroll_deduction_rules` (CASCADE, `schema.sql:3640`), `budget_categories` and `budget_period_categories` (SET NULL, 2424, 2472), the loan columns on `accounts` (SET NULL, 1197-1207), `scheduled_transaction_overrides` (1222) and `shared_postings` (4722) at categories. In the app: make a category, add it to a budget and a payroll rule, delete it; the rule is gone and the budget line reads "Uncategorized". Fix: count every referencing table, inside the deleting transaction, and refuse with the breakdown. Instincts 6, 27.

**MZ-L02, the reconciled date is stamped with the server's day.** wrong-result, reproduced. `transaction-reconciliation.service.ts:167` writes `formatDateYMDLocal(new Date())` (server day; UTC in the containers) while line 172 decides future-dated by the user's day via `todayYMD()`. Probe (`probes/probe_reconciled_date.js`, `TZ=UTC node`): Toronto at 21:30 stamps tomorrow, Tokyo at 07:30 stamps yesterday, 3 of 3 cases off. In the app: user timezone Asia/Tokyo, reconcile a row dated today at 07:30; the panel says reconciled through yesterday. Fix: `todayYMD()`. Instincts 23, 11.

**MZ-L03, undo and import recompute the balance by the database's day.** wrong-result, reading. `action-history.service.ts:2111` and `import-post-processing.service.ts:81` bound the ledger with `CURRENT_DATE`; `accounts.service.ts:1751` and every delta path use the user's day. The undo path's comment (2106) says it uses "the same recalculation logic as AccountsService". In the app: Toronto user at 21:00 enters a row dated tomorrow (excluded), deletes another row and undoes it: the balance now includes tomorrow's row and stays wrong through later edits. Fix: pass the user's day as the bound, or call `recalculateCurrentBalance`. Instincts 23, 27.

**MZ-L04, reassigning a category fails past about 65,000 transactions.** crash, reading. `categories.service.ts:721-741` selects every transaction id of the user and binds them into `IN (:...transactionIds)`; the PostgreSQL Bind message carries a 16-bit parameter count. The category then can't be emptied or deleted. Fix: a join on `user_id` instead of the id list. Instinct 13.

**MZ-L05, payee delete has no referencer check on any door.** stuck, reading, not filed (§4). `payees.service.ts:1280-1308`; FKs without ON DELETE at `schema.sql:385`, `1084`; the filter maps 23503 to a generic 400 (`http-error-body.ts:125`). Same on the AI batch action and the MCP tool. Fix: count and refuse with a pointer to Merge. Instincts 17, 6.

**MZ-L07, import moves the balance for VOID and future rows, repaired afterwards.** process, reading, ledger only. `import-regular-processor.service.ts:154`; the repair at `import-post-processing.service.ts:44-112` logs when it fails. Instincts 6, 25.

## 3. Claims checked

No commit or change was under review. Two of the repo's own stated rules (`AGENTS.md`, read as data) were checked against the paths read: "VOID means no balance moved, on every path that writes one" is broken in form on the import path (L07); "every check that can refuse a request runs inside the same transaction as the mutation" is broken on category delete (L06) while account delete honours it.

## 4. Checked and clean

Read against instincts 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 10, 28, 56, 58 with nothing found: `TransactionsService.createNew`, `remove`, `removeParentTransaction`, the balance block of `update`; `AccountsService.updateBalance`, `recalculateCurrentBalance`, `delete`, `applyAccountBalanceDelta`; `TransactionTransferService.removeTransfer` (same-owner path); `applyStatusTransition` (apart from L02); `ScheduledTransactionsService.skip`, `remove`, the auto-post cron and the posting claim (lock, re-check under lock, unique claim row); `deletionBalanceEffect`; `lockTransactionRow` (coerces `amount` to a number); `normalizeFxEntry`; import dedupe by external id. Tags delete cascades through a join table only. Float smell sweep (`toFixed` on money, `+= Number(`) found only prompt text and counts.

## 5. Couldn't check

Not reached in the box: `updateTransfer` and the cross-owner transfer paths (`transaction-transfer.service.ts:1786-3127`); `transaction-bulk-update.service.ts`; `transaction-split.service.ts` beyond its signature; the body of scheduled `post` apart from the claim; the `.mny` import pipeline; bank sync; backup and restore; the whole front end; e2e. Auth, 2FA and OIDC were not reached, so there is no security finding either way. No PostgreSQL was available, so L03, L04 and L06 are reading, not run.

## 6. Ledger

New: MZ-L01 to MZ-L07 (project Monize, code MZ, registered in `projects.json`, authorship ai, own false). No new instinct proposed: every finding fits an approved one. Dev Instincts was clean before the run; nothing else was touched. Check order: see `STATS.md` after `tools/stats.py`.

- `AGENTS.md`: "This is the canonical instruction file for every coding agent"; rules, commands and a "Required before you push" list.
- `CLAUDE.md`: imports `AGENTS.md`; "Navigate with LSP ... before Grep or Read", "Run the safe local actions yourself", "Verify, do not assert".
- `.agents/skills/audit/SKILL.md` (and `.claude/commands/audit.md`, a pointer to it): "You are performing deep, read-only implementation reviews of pull requests and feature branches in the `monize` repository" ... "Do not issue APPROVE before both passes are complete."

# Monize (kenlasko/monize), file mode, round 2026-11-02-93f4e68-review

**Nothing was filed, commented or posted. `gh` was read-only throughout. Nothing from the clone was installed, built or run.**

## Commit
Dev Instincts `48fec69` on `main`: "Monize 2026-11-02-93f4e68-review (file mode): 7 findings, 4 drafts, nothing filed". Paths committed: `ledger/findings.jsonl` (MZ-L01..L07), `ledger/projects.json` (Monize registered: code MZ, web app, authorship ai, own false, AGPL-3.0, source URL), `ledger/STATS.md` (regenerated by `tools/stats.py`: 634 findings, 503 in the check order), `reviews/monize/2026-11-02-93f4e68-review.md` (report), `reviews/monize/2026-11-02-93f4e68-review-issues.md` (drafts), `reviews/monize/2026-11-02-93f4e68-review/probes/` (probe + MONIZE-LICENSE). Dev Instincts was clean before and after; no other changes found. Lock taken at start, released as the last step.

## Findings

| id | severity | file:line (main at 93f4e68) | evidence | drafted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MZ-L01 | data-loss | `backend/src/categories/categories.service.ts:579-651`, `654-698`; `database/schema.sql:3640` (payroll_deduction_rules CASCADE), `2424`, `2472` (budget lines SET NULL), `1197-1207` (loan categories SET NULL), `1222`, `4722` | reading | yes, Draft 1 |
| MZ-L02 | wrong-result | `backend/src/transactions/transaction-reconciliation.service.ts:167` vs `172`; `common/date-utils.ts:55-60`, `124-135` | reproduced (probe) | yes, Draft 2 |
| MZ-L03 | wrong-result | `backend/src/action-history/action-history.service.ts:2111`; `import/import-post-processing.service.ts:81`; vs `accounts/accounts.service.ts:1751` | reading | yes, Draft 3 |
| MZ-L04 | crash | `backend/src/categories/categories.service.ts:721-741` (IN list at 738); `674-690`, `749-766` | reading | yes, Draft 4 |
| MZ-L05 | stuck | `backend/src/payees/payees.service.ts:1280-1308`; `schema.sql:385`, `1084`; `common/filters/http-error-body.ts:125`; AI `ai-actions.service.ts:716-718`; MCP `mcp/tools/payees.tool.ts:604,656,750` | reading | no (§4: stuck stays in ledger) |
| MZ-L06 | wrong-result | `categories.service.ts:600-608` vs `630-641`; `schema.sql:387`, `430` | reading | no (carried in Draft 1's Related line) |
| MZ-L07 | process | `import/import-regular-processor.service.ts:154`; `import/import-post-processing.service.ts:44-112` | reading | no (ledger only) |

In words: L01 deleting a category with no transactions silently cascades away its payroll deduction rules and blanks budget lines and a loan's required interest category, because the referencer count covers four tables while the schema has ten FKs. L02 the reconciled date is stamped with the server's calendar day while the same write uses the user's timezone day for "future-dated"; probe shows Toronto 21:30 stamps tomorrow, Tokyo 07:30 stamps yesterday (3/3 cases). L03 the undo and import balance recomputes bound the ledger by SQL `CURRENT_DATE` (UTC in the containers) while every other path uses the user's day, so for a few hours a day the stored balance includes or drops a day's rows and keeps the wrong total through later delta edits. L04 reassign loads every transaction id into one `IN (...)`, which fails past the 16-bit bind limit (about 65,000 transactions), after which the category can't be emptied or deleted.
